correctness.rationale: Using the published cap-barycenter support characterization, normals proportional to \((1,m)\) with \(0\le m\le1\) exhaust one octant. For \(m\le\delta/2\), direct vertical-fiber integration of the trapezoid gives \(\bar x=1-\delta/4-m^2/(3\delta)\) and \(\bar y=2m/(3\delta)\), which eliminate to the parabola. For \(m\ge\delta/2\), the right-triangle centroid gives \((1-\bar x)(1-\bar y)=2\delta/9\). Green's formula over eight symmetric sectors yields the stated logarithmic area exactly. For \(\delta>2\), the centroid identity for a cap and its complementary opposite cap gives the homothety factor \((4-\delta)/\delta\). Independent numerical cap integration and boundary-area reconstruction agree with the formulas at multiple levels, while the analytic integrations establish all levels.

value.rationale: The square is the canonical nonsmooth planar test body for a floating/metronoid transform whose literature is largely structural and asymptotic. An exact all-level boundary and area profile exposes how polygonal cap geometry changes regime and supplies a benchmark for numerical, affine, and asymptotic studies. Affine equivariance immediately extends the computation to parallelograms, so the result is more than a decorative single-parameter integral.
residual_risks: No claim is made for higher-dimensional cubes or general polygons.
